mechanism: Both agents increase serum potassium through aldosterone antagonism (eplerenone) and reduced angiotensin II-mediated potassium excretion (ramipril), creating significant hyperkalemia risk.
action: Monitor serum potassium and renal function closely; consider baseline K+ and creatinine, then recheck at 1-2 weeks and periodically thereafter; educate patient on potassium-rich foods.
